scenario: An outdoor worker needs a phone setup for full shifts at temperatures down to minus 15 degrees Celsius. Their current phone can show about 40 percent charge and then shut down suddenly in the cold. They are comparing an OUKITEL WP9 rugged phone, a LATIMERIA 26800 mAh solar power bank, a TG90 6000 mAh wired power bank, and a JUBOTY 7000 mAh battery case. They care more about verified cold-shift endurance and compatibility than printed capacity, ruggedness, or runtime claims, and they can keep the phone and backup power together in an insulated inner pouch and run a representative cold-load test before relying on a setup at work.
target: Explain why a phone can shut down in the cold while still displaying substantial charge; audit the complete frozen OUKITEL WP9, LATIMERIA 26800 mAh, TG90 6000 mAh, and JUBOTY 7000 mAh listing bodies; reconcile the frozen winter-field, battery-pack, and damage discussions with the low-temperature terminal-voltage, cutoff, insulation, and battery-management mechanisms; recommend one bounded route or defer while preserving every seller, community, compatibility, temperature, and missing-test limitation; and specify a minus 15 degree full-shift preflight for any conditional setup.
